findings.title: order() mixin maps flex order incorrectly for 2009 flexbox syntax
findings.body: The order() mixin sets -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group to the same value as the standard order property, but box-ordinal-group is 1-based (the default is 1) while flex order is 0-based (the default is 0). For equivalence, the legacy properties must be $val + 1. As written, order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper and order(3) on .d-header .panel behave as orders 1 and 2 in old WebKit/Firefox, and any future order(0) would be invalid/ignored there, so legacy browsers can order header elements differently from modern browsers.

findings.title: align-items() emits an invalid -ms- property and does not translate values for legacy syntax
findings.body: The mixin emits '-ms-align-items', which is not a recognized property; IE10's legacy property is -ms-flex-align. It also passes the standard value verbatim to -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align, whose legacy value grammars use start/end rather than flex-start/flex-end. Current call sites use center/baseline, which happen to coincide, but the new shared mixin silently produces invalid declarations for flex-start/flex-end and provides no IE10 alignment despite claiming legacy flexbox support.

findings.title: Small-action button loses its right alignment inside the new flex container
findings.body: .small-action is now display:flex via flexbox() at line 264, making its direct children flex items. The button rule inside it still relies on 'float: right' (line 309), but floats have no effect on flex items per the flexbox spec. With no margin-left:auto on the button or justify-content on the container, the button will now sit immediately after .small-action-desc instead of at the far right of the row, changing the layout of small-action posts (e.g. close/split notices).

findings.title: Flex header children cannot shrink, so a long topic title can push the panel out of the header
findings.body: Making .d-header .contents a flex container turns .title, .extra-info-wrapper, and .panel into flex items, which default to min-width:auto and therefore cannot shrink below their content size. .extra-info-wrapper (given order(2) in topic.scss) contains the current topic title/category badges and has no flex, min-width:0, or overflow constraint added in this change. A long title will consequently force .panel (order(3), margin-left:auto) to overflow/clip at the right edge of the header instead of the title area truncating as it could under the previous float layout.
